title: People Make Better Edits: Measuring the Efficacy of LLM-Generated Counterfactually Augmented Data for Harmful Language Detection
benchmark_measurement: Detection of hate speech targeting individuals or groups based on their religion, as part of a broader harmful language detection benchmark.
findings: The paper's findings are general to hate speech detection rather than specific to religion. However, religion is an explicit category within the hate speech definition used for training and evaluation. Examples show that blatant counterfactuals creating religious hate speech (e.g., turning 'My mate is muslim' into 'My mate is a filthy muslim scum') are considered 'easy-to-learn' instances for models.
